summary: A dense Pfister euro where you sail a rondel-like course around the Caribbean, juggling a personal deck of movement/action cards while building influence, cargo runs, and combat strength; a built-in narrative campaign runs alongside the economic engine. It's a lot of moving parts that click into a satisfying, if long, engine-building puzzle.
praised: multiple viable strategies and tech-track combos
the story/quest layer adds unusual narrative texture for a euro
excellent, thematic production and card-driven movement
criticised: heavy rules overhead and long teach
card draw luck affects available actions turn to turn
long playtime can drag at 4 players
can feel like solving your own puzzle with limited direct interaction

interaction.kind: competing for city control, contracts, and combat over shared spaces

scoring.why: points accumulate from influence, quests, cargo delivery, combat, and end-game bonuses all at once
